is_anopheles.evidence: The study collected and identified Anopheles gambiae (s.l.), specifically Anopheles coluzzii, Anopheles arabiensis, and Anopheles gambiae (s.s.) (Abstract and Results, Page 3).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study genotyped the L1014F (kdr-w) mutation in the sodium-gated voltage-channel gene (Page 3, Methods; Page 5, Table 2).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 2 on page 5 provides genotype frequencies (RR, RS, SS) and total sample sizes (n=122 for An. arabiensis and n=163 for An. coluzzii) for the L1014F mutation.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected using human landing catches in the village of Goden, Plateau Central region, Burkina Faso, in November 2015 (Page 2, Sampling area).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary research study reporting original entomological field collections and molecular genotyping results.

sub_country_location.evidence: Data are tied to the village of Goden (12° 25′ N, 1° 21′ W) in the Zinaré health district, Plateau Central region, Burkina Faso (Page 2).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Field collections were carried out over 12 nights in November 2015 (Page 2).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The authors mention previous studies in the same village in 2011 and 2012 (references 24 and 25), but explicitly state that the current data come from a new collection in 2015 (Page 2).

supplement.evidence: All necessary genotype counts and frequencies for the target markers are provided in Table 2 of the main manuscript.

assessment.summary: This study reports on the biting behavior and insecticide resistance of Anopheles coluzzii and Anopheles arabiensis in Goden, Burkina Faso. Mosquitoes were collected in November 2015, and a subsample of 285 individuals was genotyped for the Vgsc L1014F (L995F) mutation. The study found high frequencies of the resistant allele (66% in An. coluzzii and 38% in An. arabiensis) and observed behavioral plasticity in biting patterns despite high LLIN coverage.
